observations: The valve cover features 'CAT C9 ACERT' branding in photo 1.
An Atlas Copco brand filter is mounted on the side in photo 0.
The exhaust manifold is missing, leaving the exhaust ports on the cylinder head exposed in photo 0.
The wiring harness and Electronic Control Module (ECM) are visible.
Both photos carry a watermark for 'DNL EQUIPMENT SALES AND...'.
The background shows a workshop setting with tools and a person in orange protective clothing.

claims.evidence: Photo 0 shows the exhaust manifold is missing, leaving the cylinder head ports open.
There is no video evidence of the engine running or a diagnostic report.
Verification requires a video of the engine operating under load.
No hour meter or ECM data readout is provided.
Internal condition and previous repairs cannot be confirmed from external photos.

risks.risk: Internal mechanical failure or seized components.
risks.proof: A video clip of the engine starting and running.

risks.risk: Missing expensive bolt-on components like the turbocharger or starter motor.
risks.proof: Photos of all four sides of the engine unit.

risks.risk: Faulty or mismatched Electronic Control Module (ECM).
risks.proof: A photo of a diagnostic tool screen showing the engine serial number and status.

proof_requests: Video of the engine running to confirm it is 'working' and has 'no knock'.
Photos of the opposite side and rear of the engine to check for the turbocharger and flywheel housing.
A clear photo of the engine's metal data plate showing the serial number.
A diagnostic report or photo of the hour meter to verify usage.
response.reason: The item is identified as a Caterpillar C9 ACERT engine. The seller's claim of it being 'complete' is contradicted by the missing exhaust manifold. It is priced at the worst case as a non-working core or 'parts' engine.
